items.summary: What a 4 TiB Azure Disk Taught Us about Slow Reads One of our customers spent most of a week tuning PostgreSQL to fix slow reads. They worked through shared_buffers, effective_cache_size, work_mem, and the rest of the checklist, and set all of them sensibly. The reads stayed slow. And the reason had nothing to do with any of those settings. Their data disk had reached 4 TiB, and the moment it did, Azure switched off the host cache sitting in front of it. That is the frustrating thing about storage. Postgres sits on top of it and trusts it completely. When the disk underneath is capped, throttled, or uncached, Postgres has no way to tell you.…
items.title: Umair Shahid: Your Postgres Database Is Slow, and It Isn’t Postgres
